newsitem.title: USA: Relief group helped Bosnian Muslims get arms - report.
newsitem.headline: Relief group helped Bosnian Muslims get arms - report.

text.p: Bosnia's Moslem-led government evaded a U.N. arms embargo and purchased hundreds of millions of dollars worth of black-market weapons with the help of an obscure organisation, the Vienna-based Third World Relief Agency, the Washington Post reported in Sunday editions.

The newspaper said Austrian investigators, using documents and bank account records for the relief agency, had tracked $350 million which they said flowed from Moslem governments and radical Islamic movements to Bosnia.
At least half, according to Western intelligence estimates, was used to purchase weapons illegally and smuggle them to the Bosnian government army, the Post reported.
The headquarters of the Third World Relief Agency were raided last September by European police backed by anti-terrorist squads.

The relief agency, headed by a former Sudanese diplomat Elfatih Hassanein, has operated several civilian projects in Bosnia since 1992, including a chicken farm, a news agency and a women's sewing collective, the Post reported.

It quoted unnamed Western officials as saying Hassanein set up the organisation in 1987 and apparently turned it into the chief broker of black-market weapons deals circumventing the U.N. embargo against any arms shipments to the warn-torn former Yugoslav republic.
